title.narrative: Agricultural livelihoods support for IDPs and IDP returnees in Tigray region

description.narrative: BackgroundThe northern Ethiopia conflict (2020 -2022) displaced over a million people in Tigray, Amhara and Afar regions, leading to loss of property, livelihoods and destitution especially among the most vulnerable population. While a few IDPs have returned to their previous homes as a result of the relative calm, many remain displaced either in camps or living within host communities. The Tigray Interim Regional Administration in collaboration with the federal government plans to facilitate the return of nearly 690,000 people to Western, Northwestern and Southern zones of the region. Out of the planned number of returnees, about 69,000 people have already returned, mostly in the Southern Zone. A recent assessment mission to the contested areas of the region reported relative calm and a permissive environment to deliver humanitarian assistance to the IDPs who are in dire need of support. Emergency livelihoods assistance, including agricultural support, was one of the major needs highlighted by the IDPs and returnees. Therefore, to address the agricultural livelihood needs of the IDPs, FAO will build on its ongoing activities in the target areas and seek collaboration with other UN agencies such as IOM and UNHCR to provide critical agricultural assistance.The main objective of this project is to support IDPs, returnees and their host communities to rebuild their livelihoods and begin producing food and generating income for self-sufficiency in Tigray region of Ethiopia. This assistance will contribute to increasing food availability and accessibility, not just for the direct beneficiaries but also the communities. The project will target 36,750 IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities (7,350 households) in the target areas. With this financial support from CERF, FAO will provide quality agricultural inputs plus Cash, these inputs will include cereals, and sweet potato cuttings to enable them plant and produce food during the 2025 Meher season. The beneficiary households will also be provided with complementary agricultural extension services by the implementing partners and experts from the regional bureau of agriculture, with technical support of FAO, to enable them to adopt best agricultural practices to enhance production and productivity. Further, each of the targeted households for this intervention will be provided with one-off unconditional cash assistance of USD 100. The USD 100 unconditional cash transfer is an MPCA that should improve immediate access to food and other basic needs including paying for labour, fertilizer, vegetables seeds, medical services, school fees, etc. and mitigate the risk of resorting to negative coping strategies during the lean season. The project will also provide refresher training for 28 crop sector development agents (DAs) who will cascade the knowledge and skills to the project beneficiaries.
